name: Wälzhammer Präzision GmbH
summary: Wälzhammer is a family-owned machining shop (55 staff, 6.4 M EUR turnover, founded 1973). It is the 100 % source for our pump shaft HN 32 mm (part:320011). It is in a liquidity squeeze: credit index 302, up from 230, equity ratio 20.3 %, talks with its banks, and an MD who says the bank checks him every month. It is also short of work: the second shift has been on hold since spring and part of machining went on short-time work on 2026-09-26.

situation.decision_maker: Owner / managing director decides prices and terms personally. Inside sales handles routine quotes.

negotiation_pattern: It opens with modest asks and gives way. Mean asked +1.43 %, mean settled -1.63 %. 2025-11: asked +3.5 %, settled 0.0 %. 2024-11: offered -0.7 %, settled -3.0 %. 2023-12: asked +1.5 %, settled -1.9 %. This year it did not use the price-change notice; its 2026-09-08 quote holds 33.06 EUR and asks only for payment within 10 days. The owner offered an open-book walk-through of hourly rates and material. The MD said he cannot sign anything that lowers margin now. Under pressure on payment it pushes back: overdue-invoice letter threatening to review conditions.
wants: Fast, reliable payment: within 10 days, no late invoices
Additional volume or new parts to refill idle capacity and end short-time work
Contract continuity it can show its bank (renewal beyond 2026-12-31, longer term)
No margin erosion: price held flat
protects: unit_price: no price cut that lowers margin while the bank is watching
payment_days: will resist anything longer than today's 30 net / 10 days 3 % skonto

trades.give: payment_days: commit to guaranteed payment within 10 days on every invoice (we keep the 3 % skonto)
trades.get: unit_price held at 33.06 EUR for 2027 and fixed for 24 months, plus an OTD commitment to the 95 % target
trades.why: Cash certainty is worth far more to it than to us. We already earn 3 % skonto, about 55 % p.a. on 20 days, so reliability costs us nothing.

trades.give: contract_months: renew the framework for 24 months instead of the silent 12-month extension; volume_per_year: firm ~7,000 pcs forecast
trades.get: Small unit_price reduction (target -1 % to -2 %) backed by its own open-book calculation, or price fixed for 24 months
trades.why: Its machines are idle and the bank wants committed order intake. Volume security fills shifts without a margin cut per hour.

trades.give: volume_per_year: offer additional machined parts / RFQs to fill its free capacity
trades.get: Price reduction on part:320011 or price hold, plus lead_time_days below 28
trades.why: It said it can take extra parts at short notice. New work is the strongest lever for a hungry shop.

trades.give: Accept the price-hold quote quickly, without a long haggle
trades.get: ppm_commitment below 500 and keep chargeback at 150 EUR per complaint; tooling return clause confirmed
trades.why: Securing quality and our tooling matters more than a few cents while its solvency is uncertain.

arguments.point: We can be the customer that pays reliably within 10 days, which is predictable liquidity you can show your bank every month.
A renewed multi-year framework with a firm forecast secures order intake while machinery-sector demand is weak.
Let us take up the owner's offer to go through hourly rates and material together, so we find a price that keeps margin intact on fuller machines.
OTD of 88.9 % is still below the 95 % contract target. With the second shift idle, on-time delivery should be achievable, and we expect it in return for faster payment.

avoid: Paying late or proposing longer payment terms. It already complained about overdue invoices and threatened to review conditions.
Framing asks as a straight margin cut. The MD explicitly cannot sign that now.
Aggressive resourcing threats. They could push a fragile firm over the edge while we single-source from it.
Mentioning its bank troubles or short-time work in a condescending way. It is a family firm and will dig in if it feels disrespected.
tone: Respectful and partnership-minded, addressed to the owner/MD. Be concrete about payment reliability and volume, and stay calm and factual on OTD.
red_flags: Insolvency risk: credit index 302 (weak, up from 230), equity 20.3 %, bank negotiations, short-time work.
Single active source (100 % quota) for part:320011. Qualify the one other source and secure safety stock. We own the tooling, so confirm it can be retrieved at short notice.
OTD stuck at 85.7–88.9 % versus the 95 % target over the last three quarters.
Our late payments (47 % of invoices late) are straining the relationship and could prompt it to tighten terms.
Contract auto-extends 12 months unless notice is given 90 days before 2026-12-31, i.e. around 2026-10-02. Decide now whether to renegotiate the term.

evidence.claim: MD asked twice for earlier payment, said the bank is watching monthly, and cannot sign anything that lowers margin.
Negotiating with banks after two weak years.
Short-time work in machining due to weak order intake; second shift on hold since spring; can take extra parts at short notice.
Latest quote holds 33.06 EUR, 28 days lead time, and requests payment within 10 days.
Complained about overdue invoices and threatened to review conditions.
Owner offered an open-book review of hourly rates and material.
Past renewals settled at or below zero despite price-increase asks.
OTD 88.9 % vs 95 % target; ppm improved to 425; no overdue 8D.
Framework ends 2026-12-31, auto-extends 12 months, 90 days' notice; prices fixed per calendar year with 90 days' notice for changes.

indicators.credit_index: 302 (12 months ago 230; higher is worse, >300 weak)
indicators.scorecard_trend: 2025Q4 green (otd 96.0, ppm 1040) → 2026Q1 green (otd 88.5, ppm 623) → 2026Q2 amber (otd 85.7, ppm 720) → 2026Q3 green (otd 88.9, ppm 425)
